newsitem.title: UK: Fenchurch, Lowndes Lambert talk merger.
newsitem.headline: Fenchurch, Lowndes Lambert talk merger.

text.p: British insurance brokers Fenchurch Plc and Lowndes Lambert Group Holdings Plc said on Friday that they were considering a possible merger of the two firms.
In a joint statement, they said any merger would be based on "the relative maintainable earnings attributable to shareholders".

"The boards believe that Fenchurch and Lowndes Lambert have strong complimentary businesses and that combining them could offer significant benefits to their respective clients, employees and shareholders," the statement said.
Fenchurch had reported pre-tax profit of 4.78 million pounds ($8.07 million) for the six months to September 30, 1996 with earnings per share at 7.4 pence.
Lowndes Lambert's profit for the same period stood at five million pounds with earnings per share at 5.4 pence.

The merger talks come at a time when insurance rates have shown a consistent decline with growing competitive pressures forcing many to contemplate deals to find a way of cutting costs and achieve economies of scale.
Last month two other leading insurance brokers in the country, Lloyd Thomspon Group and JIB Group JIB said they would merge in a deal worth 300 million pounds ($1=.5922 Pound)
